verdict: REJECTED - channel pruning is not viable on this backbone
why: Every fractional cut that removes real work moves at least one of the two outputs by more than the whole fp16 conversion costs. The blocks are only 16/32/64/128 wide, so there is no removable redundancy at this scale.

whole_block_zeroing.note: sensitivity of the score map to zeroing each block's output; best 0.177 vs a 0.02 tolerance

fractional_channels.note: keep ratio 0.90/0.75/0.50 on the 8 highest-MAC blocks; needs score L1 < 0.02 AND desc cos > 0.999

convhead2 keep 0.90.note: score map BIT-IDENTICAL - it is the descriptor that breaks

the_layout_that_hid_it: ALikeNet.forward splits the head as `descriptor_map = x[:, :-1]` and `scores_map = sigmoid(x[:, -1])`. The SCORE is the LAST channel. So pruning descriptor channels leaves the score map unchanged, and a score-map-only sensitivity scan reports ZERO damage at every keep ratio while the descriptor cosine falls to 0.921. Both outputs have to be watched.
